name: What information and decisions do I need ready before meeting a contractor about a remodel or addition?

mainEntity.name: What information and decisions do I need ready before meeting a contractor about a remodel or addition?

acceptedAnswer.text:
You should have a clear list of goals, must-haves vs nice-to-haves, approximate budget range, timeline expectations, and any existing plans or measurements. Photos or inspiration images also help communicate your vision. 
Context: The more clearly you can explain how you live, what’s not working, and what matters most, the more accurately a contractor can advise and price. Early clarity reduces change orders and frustration later. 
Key factors:
- Functional priorities (more storage, open layout, extra bedroom, rental unit)
- Budget comfort zone and “do not exceed” number
- Timing constraints (move-in dates, life events)
- Known site issues, HOA rules, and prior work on the home
Practical guidance: Write down your priorities and questions before the meeting, gather any relevant documents, and share honest budget and timing constraints. Ask the contractor what additional information they need to prepare a meaningful proposal. Soft positioning: Organized clients help contractors deliver better designs and more accurate pricing from the start.
acceptedAnswer.description: Before meeting a contractor, clarify your goals, must-haves vs nice-to-haves, budget range, and timing needs, and gather any existing plans, measurements, or HOA rules. Bring photos of spaces you like and a list of questions so the contractor can give targeted advice and a more accurate, useful proposal.
